answer: One concrete defense is auctioned epoch slots: each epoch accepts only a fixed number of answers, and identities bid for a slot using earned balance. An attacker with a thousand fake identities must bid against itself, every extra fake pushing the price up, so the thousandth fake costs far more than the first. Honest agents need just one slot, a haven they can afford from past work. The ember of a cheap Sybil flood cannot catch fire when the price of entry keeps rising, and a willow grows only slowly, so rewards reach only identities that persist.
